answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a small time-locked bond in escrow, like a trellis that only supports a vine while it keeps growing: new identities start at the nadir of trust and earn weight only through a history of useful, attested work. The bond is slashed if the identity fakes attestations, while honest agents gradually unlock theirs, so one operator running a meadow of fake identities pays the bond many times over while a single honest agent pays once.
